observations: The sole causally valid pair converted an invalid control response into a valid treatment selection, improved diagnostic Span-F1 from zero to 20.4064%, reduced the first branch request by 884 tokens, and reduced the full logical path by 1,507 tokens.
The second pair also converted an invalid control response into a valid treatment selection and used 449 fewer logical tokens, but it failed H70's absolute prompt non-disclosure gate.

The triggering full read ID was not introduced by the handle state or handle tool schema. It occurred in the held terminal candidate inherited identically by control and treatment before the fork, and later became one of the treatment's private handle bindings.

Absolute absence of mapped IDs from the entire prompt confounds treatment-added disclosure with shared-prefix history. The causal cost question is whether treatment adds full IDs beyond the identical inherited prompt.

Across the two observed pairs, treatment produced two valid selections versus zero for control and used 1,956 fewer logical tokens. The frozen denominator was incomplete, so these are successor-design observations rather than an aggregate treatment estimate.
inference: H70 is rejected under its registered absolute non-disclosure contract. The evidence supports a narrower successor: retain request-local handles and exact resolution, but validate incremental non-disclosure by proving that the treatment-only state and tool schema contain zero full IDs and that every full-ID occurrence outside registered messages is identical in control and treatment. This measures added representation cost without pretending shared held history is absent.

selected_successor.name: causal incremental non-disclosure
selected_successor.mechanism: Use the unchanged request-local handle treatment, but partition the prompt into identical inherited content and registered arm-specific content. Require zero full IDs in treatment-added state and schema, exact equality of inherited full-ID occurrences across arms, exact private resolution, and the unchanged quality and token gates.

alternatives.name: translate held candidate IDs to handles
alternatives.disposition: retained if inherited full IDs themselves prove harmful; it adds a semantic-equivalence transformation that current evidence does not require

alternatives.name: single full evidence identifier
alternatives.disposition: retained but contradicted by the observed multi-file quality signal and handle token savings

alternatives.name: no transferable terminal-state gain
alternatives.disposition: retained because two incomplete development pairs cannot establish transfer

open_questions: Does incremental non-disclosure pass on a fresh fixed cohort without concealing any treatment-added full identifier?
Do inherited held-candidate IDs affect model behavior even when both branches receive them identically?
Will the two-for-two completion direction survive a complete fresh denominator?
Does the 20.4064% valid-pair Span-F1 signal replicate outside the first task?
